aAbout: EarthCam runs a network of live webcams anchored by famous places — Times Square in New York is the signature view — organised into destination pages and EarthCam TV channels that package cameras into themed streams. Alongside the free consumer network it sells professional construction-camera systems to businesses, with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse. Many public cameras are watchable free in the browser and in its mobile apps, with weather information shown alongside some cameras.
aStrengths: EarthCam is the deeper platform for famous places: a large, long-running network of scenic and tourist cameras anchored by Times Square, curated viewing through EarthCam TV, and professional construction-camera services with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse for commercial clients. For watching a specific famous place — or for a business that needs a camera installed and managed — EarthCam's camera-specific depth and history beat a nature network.
bAbout: Explore.org is a live nature and animal camera network — in its own words, 'the largest Live Nature Camera network on the planet,' claiming 200+ live cams running 24/7. Its cameras sit in natural habitats worldwide, from the Brooks Falls brown bears in Katmai, Alaska to African safaris, eagle nests, oceans and underwater scenes. It is the philanthropic multimedia division of the Annenberg Foundation, and alongside the live cams it publishes highlight reels and educational films. Viewing is on the web and through its iOS and Android apps.
bStrengths: Explore.org is the deeper nature-camera experience by far: carefully placed wildlife cameras with expert curation — the Brooks Falls brown bear cameras are the famous example — plus highlight reels, educational films and a dedicated community of wildlife watchers, all run as a philanthropic project and completely free. For watching animals live or following a season at a specific nest or river, its focused, mission-driven depth beats any generalist network.
betterAnswer: They solve different watching jobs. EarthCam is a commercial network built around famous places — landmark and travel cameras, TV-style channels and a professional construction-camera business — free to watch for the public cams. Explore.org is a free, philanthropic nature network claiming 200+ live wildlife cams, with highlights and educational films. Watch EarthCam to see a place; watch Explore.org to see an animal. Many viewers use both — and use a globe-based network when they want every kind of camera in one view.

Explore.org is better for live wildlife — bears, eagles, oceans and safaris — with curation, highlights and educational films. Neither does the other's job.

verdictA: Choose EarthCam if you want the famous views — Times Square and other landmark and travel cameras — TV-style curated channels, or professional construction-camera services for a business site.
verdictB: Choose Explore.org if you want live wildlife — bears, birds, oceans and safaris — with expert curation, highlights and education, completely free.
verdictLine: EarthCam watches places; Explore.org watches animals. EarthCam is the landmark network with a professional camera business attached; Explore.org is a free, foundation-run nature network. Pick by subject, not by features — their cameras barely overlap.
worldEye: If you want places and nature in one place, WorldEye puts 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries on a free interactive 3D globe — cities, beaches, ports, landscapes and wildlife — together with live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. There is nothing to install and no signup for the free tier, and an optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds an OSINT toolkit and intel feeds. It will not match EarthCam's construction services or Explore.org's curated bear-cam seasons, but for breadth across every kind of camera it is the larger network.
